about.title: Personal Injury Help in Angels Camp, California
about.longDescription: Angels Camp sits along Rt 49, a corridor that carries a steady mix of local traffic, tourists heading through the foothills, and commercial vehicles. Nearby routes like S Main Street, Rt 4, and Murphys Grade Road see their own share of daily travel. In the most recent full year on record, this area logged 10 injury collisions and 13 people injured, with no reported traffic deaths — numbers that reflect real people dealing with real recoveries, medical bills, and missed work. If one of those collisions involved you or someone you love, sorting out what comes next can feel overwhelming. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm — we simply connect injured people with an independent personal injury attorney who can look at the specifics of a case. There's no obligation to move forward, and if you do, the attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. Reaching out costs you nothing but a few minutes, and it can help you understand what options might be available under California law.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Soon

items.title: Time Limits Apply
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of an injury to file a claim, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity is involved. Waiting too long can close off your options entirely.

items.title: Partial Fault Doesn't Bar Recovery
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, even if you're partly responsible for what happened, you may still recover compensation — it's just reduced by your share of fault.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, so the full impact of an injury can be considered.

items.title: No Fee Unless You Win
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover money — so there's no upfront cost to find out where you stand.

items.question: Do I have to pay anything to use LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent personal injury attorney. If you choose to work with an attorney from our network, they operate on contingency, so there's no fee unless you recover compensation.

items.question: Is LawProactive a law firm?
items.answer: No. We are not a law firm and don't provide legal advice ourselves. We simply help injured people get connected with an independent attorney who can evaluate their situation.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim in California?
items.answer: Most personal injury claims in California must be filed within two years of the incident. If a government entity is involved, that deadline can be much shorter, sometimes as little as six months, so it's wise to act sooner rather than later.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster near Angels Camp?
items.answer: Public crash records for the area show that reported collisions often occur along corridors such as Rt 49, S Main Street, Rt 4, and Murphys Grade Road, with activity tending to peak on Saturdays between 3 and 5 p.m. These are simply neutral counts from public records, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, which means you can still pursue compensation even if you share some responsibility. Your recovery would just be reduced by whatever percentage of fault is assigned to you.
